proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof, bullets 3–6: integration by parts against Ψ in each coordinate direction e_i, then summation over i. Here it is stated for a general open V ⊇ tsupport Ψ.

The parent localised ∂_iG by a cutoff χ in order to apply a global integration-by-parts theorem. The pinned Mathlib theorem integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable only asks each factor to be differentiable on the topological support of the other, so the cutoff is unnecessary. Otherwise the argument is the parent's.

Notation: K := tsupport Ψ, which is compact with K ⊆ V. For y ∈ ℝⁿ, DG(y) = fderiv ℝ G y and D(DG)(y) = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ G) y.

1. (Regularity of G on V.) V is open and G is C² on V, so DG is C¹ on V (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen). Consequently:
- DG is continuous on V;
- DG is differentiable at every y ∈ V, since V is a neighbourhood of y;
- D(DG) is continuous on V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen).
For every y and all a, b, D²G(y)(a, b) = D(DG)(y)(a)(b) (iteratedFDeriv_two_apply, valid for all y).

2. (Ψ off K.) If y ∉ K, Ψ vanishes on the open neighbourhood ℝⁿ∖K of y, so Ψ(y) = 0 and DΨ(y) = 0 (support_fderiv_subset). Since Ψ is C¹, Ψ and DΨ are continuous on ℝⁿ and Ψ is differentiable everywhere.

3. (Gluing and integrability criterion.) Let f : ℝⁿ → ℝ be continuous on V with f(y) = 0 for all y ∉ K.
- f is continuous on ℝⁿ. At y ∈ V this holds because V is an open neighbourhood of y. At y ∉ V we have y ∉ K (as K ⊆ V), and f ≡ 0 on the open neighbourhood ℝⁿ∖K of y.
- support f ⊆ K and K is closed, so tsupport f ⊆ K is compact.
- A continuous, compactly supported function is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport), so f is integrable.

4. (One direction.) Fix i, and put v := e_i and g_i(y) := DG(y)v. Let ev_v : (ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ) → ℝ, L ↦ L v; it is continuous linear, and g_i = ev_v ∘ DG.
- For y ∈ V, step 1 and the chain rule show that g_i is differentiable at y with Dg_i(y)w = D(DG)(y)(w)(v).
- In particular Dg_i(y)v = D(DG)(y)(v)(v) = D²G(y)(v, v).
- g_i and y ↦ Dg_i(y)v = D(DG)(y)(v)(v) are continuous on V.

5. (Integration by parts.) Apply integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/LineDeriv/IntegrationByParts.lean) with f := Ψ, g := g_i, direction v and Lebesgue measure. Its hypotheses hold:
- y ↦ DΨ(y)v·g_i(y), y ↦ Ψ(y)·Dg_i(y)v and y ↦ Ψ(y)g_i(y) are continuous on V (steps 2 and 4) and vanish off K (step 2), so they are integrable by step 3;
- Ψ is differentiable at every point, in particular on tsupport g_i;
- g_i is differentiable at every point of tsupport Ψ = K ⊆ V (step 4).
The theorem yields ∫ Ψ(y)·Dg_i(y)v dy = −∫ DΨ(y)v·g_i(y) dy.

6. (Identify the left side.) For every y, Ψ(y)·Dg_i(y)v = Ψ(y)·D²G(y)(e_i, e_i). If y ∈ K ⊆ V this is step 4. If y ∉ K, both sides vanish because Ψ(y) = 0. Hence, for each i,
∫ Ψ(y)·D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) dy = −∫ DΨ(y)e_i·DG(y)e_i dy.   (∗)

7. (Sum over i.) For each i, the functions y ↦ DΨ(y)e_i·DG(y)e_i and y ↦ Ψ(y)·D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) = Ψ(y)·D(DG)(y)(e_i)(e_i) are continuous on V and vanish off K, so both are integrable by step 3. The integral of a finite sum of integrable functions is the sum of the integrals (integral_finsetSum). Using Ψ(y)·Σ_i c_i = Σ_i Ψ(y)c_i and (∗):
∫ Σ_i DΨ(y)e_i·DG(y)e_i dy
= Σ_i ∫ DΨ e_i·DG e_i
= Σ_i (−∫ Ψ·D²G(e_i, e_i))
= −∫ Σ_i Ψ(y)·D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) dy
= −∫ Ψ(y)·Σ_i D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) dy. ∎

theorem Submission.dorag_ha_mv_green_identity : ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid n)) (G Ψ : Euclid n → ℝ), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 2 G V → ContDiff ℝ 1 Ψ → HasCompactSupport Ψ → tsupport Ψ ⊆ V → ∫ y : Euclid n, ∑ i : Fin n, fderiv ℝ Ψ y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) * fderiv ℝ G y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) = -∫ y : Euclid n, Ψ y * ∑ i : Fin n, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 G y ![EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ), EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)] := by
  intro n V G Ψ hV hG hΨ hΨc hΨV
  have hG1 : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fderiv ℝ G) V := hG.fderiv_of_isOpen hV (by norm_num)
  have hGd : ∀ y ∈ V, DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ G) y := fun y hy =>
    (hG1.differentiableOn one_ne_zero y hy).differentiableAt (hV.mem_nhds hy)
  have hG1c : ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ G) V := hG1.continuousOn
  have hG2c : ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ G)) V := hG1.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen hV le_rfl
  have hΨ0 : ∀ y, y ∉ tsupport Ψ → Ψ y = 0 := fun y hy => image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport hy
  have hdΨ0 : ∀ y, y ∉ tsupport Ψ → fderiv ℝ Ψ y = 0 := fun y hy => by
    by_contra h'
    exact hy (support_fderiv_subset ℝ h')
  have hdΨc : Continuous (fderiv ℝ Ψ) := hΨ.continuous_fderiv one_ne_zero
  have glue : ∀ f : Euclid n → ℝ, ContinuousOn f V → (∀ y, y ∉ tsupport Ψ → f y = 0) →
      Integrable f := by
    intro f hf h0
    have hc : Continuous f := by
      rw [continuous_iff_continuousAt]
      intro y
      by_cases hy : y ∈ V
      · exact hf.continuousAt (hV.mem_nhds hy)
      · have hy' : y ∉ tsupport Ψ := fun h => hy (hΨV h)
        have : f =ᶠ[𝓝 y] fun _ => 0 := by
          filter_upwards [(isClosed_tsupport Ψ).isOpen_compl.mem_nhds hy'] with z hz
          exact h0 z hz
        exact continuousAt_const.congr this.symm
    refine hc.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport ?_
    refine IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset hΨc (isClosed_tsupport _) ?_
    refine closure_minimal (fun y hy => ?_) (isClosed_tsupport Ψ)
    by_contra h
    exact hy (h0 y h)
  have key : ∀ i : Fin n, ∫ y, Ψ y * iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 G y
      ![EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ), EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)] =
      -∫ y, fderiv ℝ Ψ y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) *
        fderiv ℝ G y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) := by
    intro i
    set v : Euclid n := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ) with hv
    set gi : Euclid n → ℝ := fun y => fderiv ℝ G y v with hgi_def
    have hgiF : ∀ y ∈ V, HasFDerivAt gi
        ((ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ v).comp (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ G) y)) y := fun y hy =>
      (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ v).hasFDerivAt.comp y (hGd y hy).hasFDerivAt
    have hgi : ∀ y ∈ V, fderiv ℝ gi y v = iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 G y ![v, v] := by
      intro y hy
      rw [iteratedFDeriv_two_apply, (hgiF y hy).fderiv]
      simp
    have hgic : ContinuousOn gi V :=
      (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ v).continuous.comp_continuousOn hG1c
    have hdgic : ContinuousOn (fun y => fderiv ℝ gi y v) V := by
      have : ContinuousOn (fun y => fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ G) y v v) V :=
        ((ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ v).continuous.comp
          (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ (Euclid n →L[ℝ] ℝ) v).continuous).comp_continuousOn hG2c
      refine this.congr fun y hy => ?_
      rw [(hgiF y hy).fderiv]
      simp
    have ibp := integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable (μ := volume) (f := Ψ)
      (g := gi) (v := v)
      (glue _ ((hdΨc.clm_apply continuous_const).continuousOn.mul hgic)
        (fun y hy => by simp [hdΨ0 y hy]))
      (glue _ (hΨ.continuous.continuousOn.mul hdgic) (fun y hy => by simp [hΨ0 y hy]))
      (glue _ (hΨ.continuous.continuousOn.mul hgic) (fun y hy => by simp [hΨ0 y hy]))
      (fun y _ => hΨ.differentiable one_ne_zero y)
      (fun y hy => (hgiF y (hΨV hy)).differentiableAt)
    rw [← ibp]
    congr 1
    funext y
    by_cases hy : y ∈ tsupport Ψ
    · rw [hgi y (hΨV hy)]
    · rw [hΨ0 y hy, zero_mul, zero_mul]
  have hint1 : ∀ i : Fin n, Integrable (fun y => fderiv ℝ Ψ y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) *
      fderiv ℝ G y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))) := fun i =>
    glue _ ((hdΨc.clm_apply continuous_const).continuousOn.mul
      ((ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ _).continuous.comp_continuousOn hG1c))
      (fun y hy => by simp [hdΨ0 y hy])
  have hint2 : ∀ i : Fin n, Integrable (fun y => Ψ y * iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 G y
      ![EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ), EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)]) := fun i => by
    refine glue _ ?_ (fun y hy => by simp [hΨ0 y hy])
    have hc2 : ContinuousOn (fun y => fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ G) y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))
        (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))) V :=
      ((ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ _).continuous.comp
        (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ (Euclid n →L[ℝ] ℝ) _).continuous).comp_continuousOn hG2c
    simp only [iteratedFDeriv_two_apply, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one]
    exact hΨ.continuous.continuousOn.mul hc2
  rw [integral_finsetSum _ (fun i _ => hint1 i)]
  simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [integral_finsetSum _ (fun i _ => hint2 i), ← Finset.sum_neg_distrib]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
  rw [key i, neg_neg]
key_steps: On the open set V, G ∈ C² gives DG ∈ C¹(V): DG is differentiable on V, D(DG) is continuous on V, and D²G(y)(a, b) = D(DG)(y)(a)(b).
Off K = tsupport Ψ, Ψ = 0 and DΨ = 0; any function continuous on V and vanishing off K is continuous with compact support, hence integrable.

For each i, integrate Ψ by parts against g_i = DG(·)e_i in direction e_i (integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable, which needs differentiability of each factor only on the other's tsupport): ∫ Ψ·D²G(e_i, e_i) = −∫ DΨ e_i·DG e_i.
Sum over i, exchanging the finite sum with the integrals since all summands are integrable.
